rationale_evidence.anchor: Nyaya treats knowledge as fundamentally relational and process-based, not as a static property of propositions.
rationale_evidence.statement: Three headline findings from applying Nyaya pramana theory, tarka, realism, and debate theory to the Kernel: (1) knowledge is relational/process-based, not a static property -- a claim is knowledge only if generated by the right kind of process (pramana) and defeasible by legitimate doubt; (2) Nyaya's two-tier epistemology (default trust in cognition vs reflective certification when doubt arises) maps onto a 'knowledge core' (trusted default) vs 'adjudication process' (certification) distinction; (3) Nyaya's theory of error is parasitic on truth (error is misplacement of properties onto the wrong object, requiring prior knowledge of the properties/object), directly relevant to the anti-reasoner concept and the representation-!=-truth problem.

Ten Nyaya observations (Part 1): (1) knowledge requires four unified factors -- knower, known, knowledge source, and knowledge itself (Nyaya-sutra 1.1.1); (2) error is parasitic on truth, a misplacement of a property onto the wrong object (Nyaya-sutra 4.2.35, the shell/silver example); (3) a two-tier epistemology of default trust vs certification when doubt arises (2.1.20); (4) pramanas (perception/inference/analogy/testimony, 1.1.3) are causes of veridical cognition, not conscious justifications -- a causal account of knowledge; (5) inference (linga) has a three-part perception->recollection->inference structure (1.1.5); (6) vyapti (invariable concomitance) must be tested in both anvaya (positive) and vyatireka (negative) directions (1.1.34); (7) absence (abhava) requires a counter-correlative (pratiyogi), you cannot assert non-existence of X without knowing what X would be if it existed (4.2.33); (8) perception is defined by four conditions (sense-object connection, language-independence, inerrancy, definitiveness, 1.1.4); (9) the lamp analogy is interpreted as mutual certification among pramanas, not self-certification (2.1.19), a coherentist element within Nyaya's foundationalism; (10) doubt (samsaya) is the catalyst for inquiry, not a failure state, arising from five distinct triggers (1.1.23).

rationale_evidence.anchor: Knowledge is a Causal Process, Not a Property
rationale_evidence.statement: Five most-surprising observations: knowledge is generated by a causal process, not possessed as a property (a Kernel might need to track the generation process/pramana, not just the claim); error requires prior knowledge of truth (opposite of the Western default-doubt assumption, so error might be modeled as a modified version of truth, not a separate category); default trust, not skepticism, is Nyaya's epistemic starting point (opposite of the Cartesian default-doubt assumption); absence is a real category with structure (counter-correlative plus type: absolute/prior/subsequent/locus-based); doubt has five distinct causal types, not just confidence degrees.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The 5 Observations Most Likely Relevant to a Minimal Knowledge Kernel
rationale_evidence.statement: Five observations ranked most kernel-relevant: the four-factor knower/known/source/knowledge relational structure (a Kernel storing only propositions loses this structure); the two-tier trusted-vs-certified structure; the parasitism thesis (error as modified truth, not a separate category); the counter-correlative requirement for absence/retraction/deletion; the five distinct doubt types (not just a confidence scalar).

p3a_pairs.what_says_this: A (S0405) contains a brief Tarka-Nyaya section (observations 11-20) using exactly the same technical vocabulary as B (abhava, vyapti/anvaya/vyatireka, nigrahasthana, paksa-sadhya-hetu, avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava). B (S0407) is a full dedicated Nyaya-sutra extraction, citing specific sutras (1.1.1 through 5.2.1), adding pramana theory (perception/inference/analogy/testimony), the two-tier trust/certification epistemology, the parasitism-of-error thesis, five doubt types, and three debate types (vada/jalpa/vitanda) that A does not contain. Both follow an identical template structure (Ten observations / Five most-surprising / Five most-relevant / Five not-actionable / Ten falsification questions / Final consolidated questions), strongly suggesting B is a follow-on, deeper treatment of the same Nyaya material A only sketched. Group-evidence G0698 (UNKNOWN-CANDIDATE-GROUP) independently treats A and B as one existing "Nyaya/Tarka falsification-lens family" when evaluating a third candidate (S0646) for possible merge.
p3a_pairs.what_would_make_this_wrong: No explicit corpus row in either sample states B extends/refines/deepens A -- this verdict rests on strong content/vocabulary overlap and template-identity (INFERRED), not a textual citation. If B were instead produced independently (e.g. by a different agent/session unaware of A, coincidentally reaching similar terminology because both cite the same Tarka-sangraha/Nyaya-sutra source texts), the relationship would be closer to CONTINUATION or even INDEPENDENT-leaning UNWITNESSED.
